patch_description: The previous generations plateaued because all four existing seeds (regular 13-gon, ellipse, perturbed polygon, uniform random) fall into the same family of near-symmetric, boundary-dominated basins, and every local-search refinement converges to ~0.02 normalized min-area. This edit adds three structurally distinct seeds that are constructed directly in the valid domain (all points inside a unit-area convex hull, so no post-hoc rescaling is needed — the failure mode that zeroed Gen 5 and Gen 9): (1) a two-cluster configuration splitting points between two arcs of the boundary, which explores asymmetric boundary layouts; (2) a Reuleaux-like rounded-square boundary with points on the curved hull, exploring a different hull shape family than polygons/ellipses; (3) a spiral fill combining an interior spiral with a few hull anchors, exploring mixed interior/boundary distributions. Each seed is built with fixed parameterization (no RNG or seeded RNG only) for determinism, and the convex hull is scaled to unit area at construction time so the returned configuration is valid-by-construction. Widening the seed set to seven distinct basins gives the downstream multi-scale refinement a materially better chance of escaping the 0.02 plateau.

def _regular_polygon_seeds(n, rng):
    seeds = []
    # regular n-gon on unit-area circle
    R = (1.0 / (0.5 * n * np.sin(2 * np.pi / n))) ** 0.5
    pts = np.array([[R * np.cos(2 * np.pi * i / n), R * np.sin(2 * np.pi * i / n)] for i in range(n)])
    seeds.append(("regular_%dgon" % n, pts.copy()))
    # ellipse-perturbed variant
    a, b = 1.3, 1.0 / 1.3
    pts2 = np.array([[R * a * np.cos(2 * np.pi * i / n), R * b * np.sin(2 * np.pi * i / n)] for i in range(n)])
    hull_area2 = 0.5 * n * R * R * a * b * np.sin(2 * np.pi / n)
    pts2 = pts2 / np.sqrt(hull_area2)
    seeds.append(("ellipse_%dgon" % n, pts2.copy()))
    return seeds
